messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING @aaron_oncall — Multiple Xid/driver-reset events detected on serving-prod-us-west-2 (shard-r5). Severity: P2. Autoscaler has shifted some pods; observed node flaps and container crashes. Logs show `NVRM: Xid (79) GPU fault`. Please triage.

aaron_oncall: ack — I'm on it. Seeing a spike in driver resets and OOM restarts. Which nodes?

maya_engineer: reporting from logs: nodes gpu-r5-07,gpu-r5-09 hit repeated Xid(79) over last 8m. dmesg snippet: ```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (79) 00000000 0x00000000 0x00000000
[ 1234.567900] NVRM: Xid (79) GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568000] kernel: pid 4421 (model-server), uid 1001: killed by SIGKILL - oom_killer
```

lia_infra: quick infra note — gpu-r5-07 shows ECC correctable count rising then a driver reset. nvml reports ECC=correctable spikes. Suspect thermal or hardware glitch but need to mitigate customer impact asap.

aaron_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) cordon + drain gpu-r5-07 and gpu-r5-09 2) scale up fallback pool (cpu-only or smaller quantized model) 3) restart nvidia-driver on recovered nodes and monitor for recurrence. Who can run the drain?

lia_infra: I'll run the drain. Command I'll use: `kubectl cordon gpu-r5-07 && kubectl drain gpu-r5-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=10m` — will do one node at a time.

james_support: Customer impact: Support signals 3 customers reporting 503s in the last 12m — bucketed to requests hitting shard-r5 -> large generation jobs timing out. Notifying affected customers: finlytics-app, lexicon-ai. ETA to notify: 10m after we confirm mitigation.

maya_engineer: also toggling runtime fallback in routing policy: temporarily route heavy gen to model-x-small-quant (lower perf but stable) and keep canary for standard model off. Patch: `routing.set_fallback("serving-prod", "model-x-small-quant")` — rolling now.

lia_infra: drain started on gpu-r5-07. Pod evictions in progress. Node shows one more Xid but no new OOMs after throttling batch size on that node.

aaron_oncall: good. After drain completes, I'll run `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service` and collect `nvidia-smi --query` + `dmesg` and hold node cordoned until 30m stable.

incident-bot: Incident timeline: 1845009800 initial spike detected -> 1845009876 paging -> 1845009940 drain started -> 1845010200 fallback routing applied -> 1845010400 customer notices opened.

maya_engineer: quick config we changed to mitigate batching impact: `INFER_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=512 -> 256` for model server on shard-r5 to reduce memory pressure.

james_support: sent preliminary customer bulletin to finlytics-app and lexicon-ai: "We are investigating degraded latency/restarts affecting some inference requests. Engineers are mitigating; we'll share an update within 30 minutes."

aaron_oncall: handoff plan: I'm going to monitor for 20 more minutes; if stable, I'll uncordon one node at a time and watch metrics. @mira_oncall — on next shift please take over monitoring and follow the runbook at https://intra.redwood/runbooks/gpu-xid-ecc. Key actions: keep fallback routing, do not uncordon until 30m stable post-driver restart, escalate to hw team for any repeat Xid within 1h.

mira_oncall: acked, taking handoff in 15m. I'll verify evictions completed and keep watch on ecc/correctable counters.

lia_infra: drain finished for gpu-r5-07, starting drain gpu-r5-09 now. No new container restarts on drained pods.

aaron_oncall: pushing a short postmortem stub to incidents channel once stable. Reactions: :thumbsup: :eyes:

incident-bot: Note: Automated mitigation triggered — routing fallback engaged and autoscaler brought up 2 ephemeral CPU-backed replicas to handle overflow.

mira_oncall: I'll update `last_message_ts` and close loop once both nodes are back in rotation or replaced.

james_support: will wait to send final customer update after your confirmation.

aaron_oncall: closing monitoring window for now — leaving handoff note to @mira_oncall.
